newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Santa Fe looks for oil in Ghana, Keta Basin.
newsitem.headline: Santa Fe looks for oil in Ghana, Keta Basin.

text.p: Houston-based Santa Fe Energy Resources Inc has signed an agreement with the government of Ghana to look for oil and gas offshore in the Keta Basin and onshore, near the border with Togo.
Under the terms of the agreement, signed late on Wednesday, Santa Fe will invest $10 million over the next three years in the project, exploration manager Tim Parker said.

"We expect to drill a well late 1999 or beginning 2000. We would not undertake this kind of investment unless we believe there is a good chance of getting oil and gas at the Keta Basin," Parker told Reuters.
Santa Fe is also engaged in exploration projects in Ivory Coast and Gabon in Africa, as well as in Argentina, Ecuador, Indonesia and China.

Two other small U.S. oil companies, Hunt Oil and Nuevo/Yukong, plus Britain's Dana Seafield, have been granted concessions over the past two years off Ghana, but all in the Tano Basin, near the western border with Ivory Coast.
